The moat stands dead flat, brimming exactly to its lip, doubling every tower upside down in perfect blue, each inverted turret hanging motionless below.
A canal runs fast and heavy with sand in it, the water gone amber-brown, grains tumbling over one another along the cut face of the bottom.
The sea comes in over flat sand as a thin fast advancing skin, cobalt deepening to near-black where it presses toward the outermost wall along the far border.
One pool has gone so still that the shovel's impression on its bottom is visible through six centimetres of perfectly clear water, every grain in place.
Water falls from the highest pool to the next in eight small bright steps, each drop striking and sending a ring outward before the next one arrives.
The moat is draining out through a gap, cutting itself deeper as it goes, the exposed wet floor darkening to near-black in a fast-spreading stain behind the current.
Foam rides into the moat in a lace of tight bubbles, one fleck of it turning slowly in an eddy at the north corner, completing its fourth full circuit.
The wet sand right to the frame's edge holds the whole sky, mirror-bright and unbroken, the structure standing on its own reflection without any seam.
Water pushes up through the canal floor from below, the whole bed darkening at once in a slow dark bloom spreading outward from the centre.
Three linked pools stand level and still, each holding a different piece of sky — the leftmost pale grey-blue, the middle deep cobalt, the rightmost blazing white.
A spillway carries water down the outer ramp in a moving skin, so thin it goes transparent at its edges and the wet sand shows amber through it.
The sand along the moat's inner wall is pocked all over with the small craters of sinking bubbles, each crater's rim a slightly darker ring in the damp surface.
Water is sinking into the far end of the canal faster than it arrives, the sand there going from deep brown back through amber to pale gold as the minutes pass.
The moat brimming to its lip carries one long thread of green weed that turns slowly in no apparent current, completing one full revolution every thirty seconds.
A low white line of breaking water moves along the bright border at the frame's edge, foam hissing forward across flat sand before thinning and disappearing into it.
Wet sand goes pale in a widening band outward from the dam's base, the near-black retreating in real time, the dry sand advancing grain by grain behind it.
The canal's surface wrinkles in the wind so the reflections of the towers break into bright gold and blue stripes running lengthwise with the current.
The moat is down to a dark stripe of wet in its own bottom, the walls above it showing a tide line of stranded foam-grit at the high-water line.
Water seeps out of the wall's base in a dark spreading stain, moving outward through the sand without any visible source, the wet front advancing in a slow arc.
One pool so still that one drip's rings are still crossing it, the outermost ring just reaching the wall and sending back the faintest second ring inward.
The sea sits as one saturated cobalt band along the far border, everything else running pale and wet out of frame toward it, the bright water band hard above.
A tide line of stranded foam and shell grit runs along the wall's base, each fragment pressed flat into wet sand that is beginning to pale as it dries.
The highest pool overflows its near lip, the overflow so slow it does not break but simply slides over the edge and disappears into the sand below the ramp.
Sand grains tumble over and over along the moat's floor in the arriving current, each one catching light for a moment before settling and being lifted again.
The whole flat apron of sand surrounding the dam stands near-black and mirror-bright, the structure's reflection extending outward from every wall simultaneously in deep indigo and white.
